source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Seed soaking and incubation before sowing (SRI method): before soaking, first do a preliminary germination test on a small sample of the seed lot. The quantity of good seed needed is 10-15 kg per hectare (a much lower seeding rate than conventional broadcasting). Put the seed into a sack and soak it in clean water for 24 hours. After soaking, wash the seed clean, then pile the wet seed inside the sack to a depth of 10-15 cm and cover the top of the pile to help it incubate. During incubation, turn the sack (flip the pile from top to bottom) every 12 hours, and lightly sprinkle it with water as needed to keep it moist, until the seed sprouts evenly.

Sowing onto the seedbed: sow the sprouted seed evenly over the bed at a rate of about 100 grams per square meter. The source slides give this rate with a parenthetical traditional-measure equivalent transcribed as "1 tuk-dai" (ទូកដេ); this local unit name could not be confidently translated and is noted here only for reference - rely on the 100 g/sqm figure. Sow in the late afternoon/evening to avoid seedling stress from daytime heat. If rain is expected, it is better to delay sowing until after the rain has passed, so that the sown seed does not wash together into clumps or get carried into drainage channels.
